# ww3-gpu: the WW3 GPU Lab

> ww3-gpu makes the WAVEWATCH III (WW3) ocean wave model run faster with Kokkos and CUDA, without changing the Fortran's arithmetic: each translated routine must give the same bits as the Fortran routine it replaces, in the same WW3 executable. It is a one-person research project of h0ffmann (Matheus Hoffmann), done with LabECO/UFSC and written up as a UFRJ/DEL project proposal and a preprint.

This file is an index for language models and for people, in the format of https://llmstxt.org. It lives at the root of https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu and the website serves it at https://wave.piabrota.art/llms.txt. Each link has one short note; the detail is behind the link. When this file and a linked file disagree, the linked file is right, and for any statement about WW3 itself the source is WW3's `model/src` at the commit ww3-gpu pins, not this file. The list of other work was read from GitHub on 2026-11-11 and names public repositories only.

## Start here

- [README](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/README.md): what the lab is, in one minute, with its study areas and their state. Portuguese mirror: README.pt-BR.md.
- [Website](https://wave.piabrota.art/): the front page (research, numbers, tools, figures, port, decisions, designs, how to cite) and the lineage page, built from this repository's files at a pinned commit.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/AGENTS.md): the repository's invariants (bit for bit with the Fortran, WW3 is read-only, translate don't improve, evidence on every claim) and where each kind of change belongs.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): the longer form of those rules, including whether WW3 itself is deterministic enough for bit-for-bit comparison.

## The port

- [kokkos/README.md](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/kokkos/README.md): the C++/Kokkos port, why Kokkos, how a routine is wired into WW3 behind a switch.
- [kokkos/PORT_STATUS.md](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/kokkos/PORT_STATUS.md): the port ledger and the port score (how much of WW3's run time and code is translated, ported and regtested), written by `scripts/port_score.py`. A text that contradicts it is wrong.
- [kokkos/PORT_TABLE.tsv](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/kokkos/PORT_TABLE.tsv): every routine translated, claimed or timed, the next port first.
- [kokkos/port_report/](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/tree/main/kokkos/port_report): one report per ported routine: what was ported, its benchmarks and how it was regtested.
- [bench/README.md](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/bench/README.md): how a timing is taken and recorded; a timing enters a table only after WW3's regtests pass on its commit.
- [regtests/](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/tree/main/regtests): the CMake/CTest driver that runs WW3's own regtest matrix, Fortran routine against Kokkos routine.
- [ww3-dia-gpu-v2](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-dia-gpu-v2): an earlier deliverable, the whole W3SNL1 (DIA nonlinear interactions) inside WW3, bit for bit. Archived.

## Decisions, designs and records

- [docs/ADRs.md](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/docs/ADRs.md): the numbered architecture decisions, with status and date.
- [docs/WFIPs/README.md](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/docs/WFIPs/README.md): the design proposals (WFIPs), each tied to a deliverable of the project proposal.
- [docs/log/](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/tree/main/docs/log): dated entries of what was tried, negative results included.
- [notes/index.md](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/notes/index.md): the ideas the lab stands on.
- [docs/ww3-manual/README.md](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/docs/ww3-manual/README.md): WW3's manual (version 7.14) summarised by topic, as a map to the source.
- [docs/GLOSSARY.md](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/docs/GLOSSARY.md): every abbreviation, switch, routine and tool name used in the repository.

## Texts

- [Preprint](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/pubs/preprint/README.md): the paper on wave models on GPUs, in English and Brazilian Portuguese, with its Markdown source.
- [Project proposal](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/tree/main/pubs/proposal): the UFRJ/DEL undergraduate project proposal, co-advised at LabECO/UFSC; `pt/` is the reference text, `en/` its mirror.

## Cite and releases

- [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/CITATION.cff): how to cite the software; the README's "How to cite" section has the formatted citation.
- [RELEASES.md](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/RELEASES.md): the releases and what each changed.
- [RELATED_WORK.md](https://github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu/blob/main/RELATED_WORK.md): the works this one cites or runs beside.

## Other research and personal work of h0ffmann

- [All the work of h0ffmann](https://github.com/piabrota/nix-os/blob/main/llms.txt): the full index of his public work, kept in piabrota/nix-os.
- [GitHub profile](https://github.com/h0ffmann) and [website](https://h0ffmann.github.io/h0ffmann/): the timeline, the works and how they connect.
- [chaceon](https://github.com/h0ffmann/chaceon): CPU and GPU wave modelling in Rust, written by agents.
- [picasso](https://github.com/h0ffmann/picasso): deterministic toolchains with just, Nix and Rust; ww3-gpu's Fortran/MPI/NetCDF toolchain is pinned from it. Pages: https://h0ffmann.github.io/picasso/.
- [proof](https://github.com/h0ffmann/proof): write what you can do, do what you write; its pages are at https://proof.piabrota.art/.
- [closed-source](https://github.com/h0ffmann/closed-source): a book on why closed source failed as a protection. Site: https://closed.piabrota.art/.
- [nashkell](https://github.com/h0ffmann/nashkell): game theory in Haskell. Pages: https://h0ffmann.github.io/nashkell/.
- [sharingan](https://github.com/h0ffmann/sharingan): when Aider meets an instruction DSL.
- [awesome-ocean-science](https://github.com/h0ffmann/awesome-ocean-science): a list of ocean-science resources.
- [forecast-energy-demand](https://github.com/h0ffmann/forecast-energy-demand): forecasting algorithms applied to hourly electricity demand.
- [astrbot_dw_ext_br_south_disaster](https://github.com/h0ffmann/astrbot_dw_ext_br_south_disaster): disaster alerts for the South of Brazil (RS, SC, PR), an extension of an AstrBot plugin.
- [astrbot_dw_ext_br_south_waterq](https://github.com/h0ffmann/astrbot_dw_ext_br_south_waterq): bathing-water quality alerts for the South of Brazil, an extension of the same plugin.
- [gcp-agentic-architect](https://github.com/h0ffmann/gcp-agentic-architect): learning agents on GCP.
- [awesome-agentic-ai](https://github.com/h0ffmann/awesome-agentic-ai), [awesome-neurosymbolic-ai](https://github.com/h0ffmann/awesome-neurosymbolic-ai), [awesome-prediction-markets](https://github.com/h0ffmann/awesome-prediction-markets): curated lists.
- [okekara](https://github.com/h0ffmann/okekara): synchronized lyrics and a karaoke mode for YouTube Music.
- [swim-sync](https://github.com/h0ffmann/swim-sync): a swim training app.
- [chemo-rx](https://github.com/h0ffmann/chemo-rx): his undergraduate thesis.

## marola-dev: the water super app

- [marola.dev](https://marola.dev): the live map: nearby beaches, sea and weather, bathing-water quality and a 0 to 100 swimability score. marola is the second consumer of ww3-gpu.
- [marola](https://github.com/marola-dev/marola): the umbrella repository: the design proposals (MIPs), the ways of working and every code repository as a submodule. Docs: https://docs.marola.dev/.
- [marola-app](https://github.com/marola-dev/marola-app): the backend.
- [marola-site](https://github.com/marola-dev/marola-site): the marola.dev frontend.
- [marola-ml](https://github.com/marola-dev/marola-ml): marolaGPT, its fine-tune, the DSPy prompt compile, the local model image and the benchmark gate.
- [marola-research](https://github.com/marola-dev/marola-research): the research of the project. Pages: https://marola-dev.github.io/marola-research/.
- [marola-corpus](https://github.com/marola-dev/marola-corpus): sourced ocean and marine-safety notes, released as a pinned tarball.
- [marola-oods](https://github.com/marola-dev/marola-oods): the open ocean data store, Brazilian bathing-water data as versioned files.
- [marola-devkit](https://github.com/marola-dev/marola-devkit): the development harness: scripts, a Claude Code plugin marketplace and reusable workflows.
- [marola-skills](https://github.com/marola-dev/marola-skills) and [marola-agents](https://github.com/marola-dev/marola-agents): the skills and agents of the marola repositories.
- [awesome-ocean-sciences](https://github.com/marola-dev/awesome-ocean-sciences): a curated list of ocean-science software, models, data and resources.

## piabrota: the AI studio

- [www.piabrota.art](https://www.piabrota.art/): the studio's site. Its own index for agents: https://www.piabrota.art/llms.txt.
- [nix-os](https://github.com/piabrota/nix-os): the NixOS configuration of the servers that host piabrota.art, wave.piabrota.art included.
- [mu](https://github.com/piabrota/mu): the company chart: the dogma, the standards, the journal and the index of the repositories.
- [pirsig](https://github.com/piabrota/pirsig): an agentic second brain.
- [rax](https://github.com/piabrota/rax): an agentic runtime on Kubernetes, in Rust.
- [agents](https://github.com/piabrota/agents): piabrota's agents.
- [skills](https://github.com/piabrota/skills): piabrota's skill set. Site: https://skills.piabrota.art/.
- [gramatico](https://github.com/piabrota/gramatico): Brazilian Portuguese on rails. Pages: https://piabrota.github.io/gramatico/.
- [room](https://github.com/piabrota/room): a personal site that is a 3D room, with camera shots, VHS tapes and a lofi radio. Site: https://room.piabrota.art/.
- [alerts](https://github.com/piabrota/alerts) and [dojo](https://github.com/piabrota/dojo): the alerts realm and the dojo.

## ouroboric-dev: open factories that improve themselves

- [ouroboric](https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/ouroboric): the charter, standards, journal and brand.
- [yggdrasil](https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/yggdrasil): an open software factory where agents build and humans steer. Design phase.
- [asgard](https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/asgard): the company factory, running on Yggdrasil. Design phase.
- [odin](https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/odin): the orchestrator: the graph engine and the ygg CLI.
- [gungnir](https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/gungnir): the contract: Go interface types and JSON schemas for ledger events and the graph, pack and factory files.
- [jormungandr](https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/jormungandr): the loop: build, check and fix with attempts, backoff, budgets and escalation.
- [gleipnir](https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/gleipnir): the harness: agent adapters, the devcontainer sandbox driver, policies and the check runner.
- [voluspa](https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/voluspa): the graph library, one folder per graph with its stage prompts.
- [havamal](https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/havamal): the skill library, vendored and own skills with their evals.
- [mimir](https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/mimir): the public benchmark kit: briefs, task format, sample suites and results.
- [helheim-go](https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/helheim-go), [midgard-react](https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/midgard-react), [niflheim-local](https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/niflheim-local): the realm flavours for Go backends, React frontends and one machine with no cloud.
- [ouroboric-packages](https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/ouroboric-packages): the placeholder packages on PyPI and crates.io that hold the project's name.
